title: DX12 transient/general pools need coordinated empty-cache reclamation under pressure
body:
Followup to #11130 and #9818. Separate general and transient allocators reduce measured retention, but each can retain empty native heaps. An allocation in one pool can fail while reclaimable cached heaps remain in the other. gpu-allocator's recovery within one Allocator cannot see the sibling pool.

The reviewed implementation releases the allocating pool's lock before reclaiming the other pool's empty caches, then reacquires the original pool and retries. It never holds both locks together and does not reclaim occupied allocations. The single-pool alternative was measured: it increases reservation in two workloads, so #11130's lifetime separation is still justified. This is independent of the standalone native-resource rollback defect https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/issues/11142.

The prepared cross-pool patch depends on gpu-allocator APIs proposed in Traverse-Research/gpu-allocator#323. They are not released. Therefore no production path/git dependency override, invented version, or non-compiling PR is being submitted. The patch, dependency pins and reproducible comparison are preserved in the evidence bundle; it should become a PR when a compatible allocator release can be selected. Merge order: allocator APIs and release, then a normal dependency update plus cross-pool recovery. This is a genuine dependency blocker, not a request to merge #11130 with an unreleased dependency.

Agent-assisted investigation and report. Evidence: https://github.com/simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/tree/main/allocator-reconciliation-20261128
